# Pilot lab fixtures

Answers Tally gave on 2026-10-09 on the synthetic company `BRIDGE PILOT LAB` (TallyPrime 7.1
Silver, licensed mode), sent by an outside contributor from a machine of their own, one request at a
time, each answer written straight to a file with `curl.exe -o` and never piped. The company was
the only one loaded. The contributor published the answers on the branch `lab/1342-capture-answers` (commit
`4bceb5d0`) with a hash table; each file here is byte-equal to the file there and its SHA-256
equals the one in that table.

The data is synthetic: the company, its GSTIN (of the synthetic family the fixtures may carry)
and its ledgers were made for this measurement. One book, one release, one day.

## The invoice round (2026-10-09)

The one-invoice round of #1342, sent by the same contributor on the same company, the same way: one request at a time, each answer written straight to a file with `curl.exe -o`. The answers are on `lab/1342-capture-answers` (the third-round reads in `fixed3/` at commit `0b85a64c`, the invoice round in `post/` at commit `01cbee0b`); each file here is byte-equal to the file there, and its SHA-256 equals the one in that branch's hash table. The book is the one the third-round reads describe: ten keyed vouchers dated 2026-08-01, then `BP/26-27/0010`, imported once from `pilot-lab-invoice-post-request.utf16le.xml`, which ComplyEaze Bridge's own build rendered from these answers (REMOTEID `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000777`).

`pilot-lab-number-new-invoice.utf16le.xml` and `pilot-lab-invoice-readback-before-post.utf16le.xml` are the same bytes: two requests whose answer was an empty collection of this company, which reads the same whatever the request.

The company's tax units were first read with a request typed by hand and sent as UTF-8 (the same collection under another name, before any voucher was keyed); that answer is not kept here, because it answers a request other than the one the code sends. `pilot-lab-tax-units.utf16le.xml` answers the code's own request.

## The voucher-numbering round (2026-10-16)

The build and the post each read the voucher-type numbering of the company before they go on (#724; `fetch_voucher_type_numbering`): the voucher types with their master ids and AlterIDs, then the same types with their series-level numbering, each read as a pair. The lab was not asked those two requests on 9 Oct, so they were read on 16 Oct 2026, read-only, from the same company on the same machine as the rest of the set (BRIDGE PILOT LAB, GUID `6b43e498-430c-4d5c-bfef-d32e2ab93c85`, created on the PC the 9 Oct answers came from), with Claude Desktop closed and each request sent once per send of the pair, one at a time, the answer written straight to a file. Both sends of each pair were byte-identical. By then the book had moved on: its marks read `ALTVCHID` 68 and `ALTMSTID` 245 (the replay serves 16/17 and 223), and it held three voucher types made after the invoice round (the zero-value types of the W-list: `BRIDGE Sales Two` with AlterID 245, `BRIDGE Sales Z1` 230, `BRIDGE Sales Z0` 228). The two files below are the answers whole, as received; the replay in `agent_import_post_e2e_tests.rs` serves them with exactly those three rows removed (every removed row carries an AlterID above the replay's master mark 223, and the test counts and names them), because the code refuses a numbering read whose types are newer than its mark. What is left after that removal is taken to be what the book held at mark 223, and that is an inference: the 25 rows left equal the 9 Oct voucher-types capture (`pilot-lab-voucher-types.utf16le.xml`, the replay's `T` read) in name, AlterID and GUID, and a test asserts it; `BRIDGE Sales` (AlterID 212, GUID ending `-000000ce`) is among them. The series-level fields of those rows (the numbering method of the series, prevent-duplicates) have no 9 Oct capture to compare with, so for them the inference is not checked. Where the bytes came from: the lab session that ran the reads on 16 Oct 2026 kept the answers as `ans-r18-1` and `ans-r19-1` (the second sends, `ans-r18-2` and `ans-r19-2`, are byte-identical) beside the two request files and a record of their hashes; they are not on a published branch, and the files here are those bytes (sha256 in the table).
